head: pr17457-r14
report:
NO DEFECTS

I found no defect I can prove at this head. I ran no probes or tests in the 20 minutes: everything below comes from reading the diff and the snapshot source, so none of it has been measured. The diff is about 24,400 lines and I read only the hold mechanism and the code behind each earlier finding. The test-only ownership checker (`model-request-ownership.ts`) I did not reread at all.

## NOT A DEFECT

**Earlier findings, status at this head (from reading the code, not from running it):**

| Earlier finding | Status | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Claude N1: Anthropic `coworkFetch` uses `node:https` and skips the hold | Closed in code | `sendCoworkRequest` now calls `admitSend(signal)` right before `https.request`, with no await between. The fallback is `gatedFetch()`. The over-https retry case was not re-run. |
| Claude N2: `withAuth` resolves the key, and can start a refresh, before checking the hold | Closed in code | `withAuth`, `withOAuthAccess`, `resolveRetryKey` and `runOAuthAttempt` now check the hold before resolving or attempting. Refreshes start through `SharedFlight.start`, and `admitSharedStart` refuses a held caller (`refresh.ts:940,1137`). |
| Claude N3: worker threads; N7: child processes | Open, now documented as not covered | Both are listed in the `request-hold.ts` header among the paths the hold does not cover. |
| Claude N4: checker cannot see `node:https`; F4d: `.es6` extension | Not rechecked | I did not reread the checker. |
| Claude N5: `AuthBrokerClient` keeps the fetch it saw at construction | Closed in code | A `#fetch` getter now reads `globalThis.fetch` on every request. `AuthStorage`'s usage fetch was changed the same way. |
| Claude N6 / Astra P1b: putting the global fetch back ends the hold | Partly closed | It is documented. `ensureRequestHoldFetch()` wraps the global again when a hold engages (`#stopForDisposingOwner`). The library's own transports now check the hold themselves, whatever `globalThis.fetch` is. |
| Claude R10-LATE-SURVIVOR: a job registered after its owner began disposing stays held for ever | Closed for the reported shape | `bindOwnerDisposal` cancels held jobs when the binding is released or replaced. Remaining gap, not exercised: a job registered after that release is not held at all, because no binding is left. I have no caller that does this, so I am not asserting it. |
| Astra P1: Cursor sends over HTTP/2 after the hold | Closed for the session and the run request | `admitSend` runs in the same turn as `http2.connect` and `client.request`, in both the proxy and direct branches. The request body is written synchronously at `cursor.ts:1793`; I read through to it and found no await on the way. Later frames on an open stream are not checked, which matches the documented rule that a response already under way runs to completion. |
| Astra P2: a shared reset fails when the caller that started it is cancelled | Closed in code | `resets.ts:128,226` now use `SharedFlight`, which runs the work on its own signal and aborts it only when no caller is still waiting. |
| Astra P2: new checker bypass forms | Not rechecked | |

**Suspicions I ruled out:**
- **`yieldQueue.close()` in `beginDispose` could make job-result deliveries retry until timeout.** It doesn't: `#deliverAsyncJobResult` returns early when the session is disposed (`agent-session.ts:3638,3646`), so the sink never sees a rejection.
- **One session disposing a shared `CacheWarmer` could switch warming off for others.** Not possible: `sdk.ts:4634` creates one warmer per session.
- **Shared work started by `SharedFlight` might still run inside the first caller's hold.** Every call site wraps the work in `runOutsideRequestHold`.
- **Removing `timeoutMs` from `usage.report` / `health.ts` could leave probes without a timeout.** `#fetchUsageUncached` now applies the service's own `requestTimeoutMs`.
- **The `remote-store` usage reload after an invalidation might run inside a hold.** The `.then` callback keeps the shared-work context it was created in, so `admitSharedStart` lets it start.
- **`fetchWithRetry` now stops on a hold refusal.** A request aborted because the hold engaged before its response arrived is not a refusal, so it is retried and the retry then waits held. That is the documented design.
- **Job registration now lists the job with a placeholder `Promise.resolve()` before its body runs.** This only matters if something synchronous inside the body waits on all jobs. I found no such path, so I am not asserting it.
